tests.description: echo maps to print, so a command that used to need a human approval now raises no interrupt at all.
Redirected, the same echo is a file write, which `write` already gates. `dir` is never empty, because `write` rejects an empty one.
Quotes delimit a word, they are not part of its value, and adjacent parts concatenate into one word.
`echo -n` drops the trailing newline and `-e` interprets escapes; mapping either would print something bash never would, so both go to bash.
Bare `echo` still prints a newline, not nothing.
Each git subcommand maps onto the std::git tool that answers the same question.
`--staged` is a different question from a bare `git diff`, so the flag has to reach the action rather than being dropped on the way.
An unrecognized flag falls back rather than being ignored: answering `git log --graph` with a plain gitLog() would give the model something other than what it asked for.
A command with no equivalent tool still runs, as a bash action, with the approval that implies.
In a sequence, the command handed to bash is the one that fell through, rendered back from its own AST, not the whole string.
Commands separated by `;` each become their own action.
makeActions reports what each command WOULD do; which side of a `&&` or `||` actually runs is decided at run time.
Bash scopes a leading assignment to its one command, and handing the original text to bash reproduces that exactly.
An explicit file descriptor, an input redirect, and a redirected git command all fall back rather than being approximated.
Anything bash would rewrite before the command runs is rejected by the parser rather than reaching makeAction. Quoted, a glob is ordinary text and still maps.
tests.expectedOutput: [["REFUSED: Unexpected input after commands: \"*\""],["REFUSED: Unexpected input after commands: \"~/d\""],["REFUSED: Unexpected input after commands: \"$(date)\""],["REFUSED: Unexpected input after commands: \"| grep x\""],["REFUSED: Unexpected input after commands: \"&\""],["print"]]

tests.description: An unset variable passes NO argument in bash where expanding it to "" would pass one, so an unquoted empty word falls back. Quoted, it is a real empty argument.
`echo ""` passes one empty argument, so it prints a newline rather than falling back.
A failure stops the sequence and reports which command failed and why, what already ran, the output so far, and what never ran.
tests.expectedOutput:
"Command `git log --graph --nope` failed: `git log --graph --nope` was not run: interrupt rejected

Commands run:
echo one

Output so far:
<results>
one

</results>

Commands not run:
echo three"

interruptHandlers.expectedMessage: Are you sure you want to run this shell command?

tests.description: `a && b` does not run b when a fails, and the chain fails as a whole.

tests.description: The caller's cwd lands on every action a command produces — a write's dir, a git action's cwd, and a bash fallback's cwd — not only on the unparseable path.
When the left side of `&&` succeeds and the right fails, the left side really ran, so its output stays in the failure report.
tests.expectedOutput:
"Command `echo kept && git log --graph --nope` failed: `git log --graph --nope` was not run: interrupt rejected

Output before the failure:

"
